quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 guidance (CFO Joseph Tung, NT dollar terms, FX assumption USD 1 = NT$31.8): consolidated revenue +7%-9% QoQ, consolidated gross margin +20-100 basis points QoQ, consolidated operating margin +50-120 basis points QoQ; EMS revenue to grow at least 10% YoY with EMS operating margin similar to Q2 2025 levels. ATM margins: sequential improvement expected to continue, with second-half ATM gross margin to reach the upper end of the structural gross margin range; the Q2 improvement is partly offset by higher costs of early resource deployment for product transitions. CFO: ASE's 'strong market position continues to support a favorable pricing environment throughout the year'; cost increases from market uncertainties 'can be fully passed through', while pricing is set to reach ASE's margin requirement. Closing remark: 'Come next year, when these things are more settled, we will be reviewing our structural margin range'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 consolidated revenue +7%-9% QoQ; GM +20-100 bp; OM +50-120 bp; EMS revenue +at least 10% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: CAPEX AND CAPACITY: CFO Joseph Tung is raising 2026 capex by an additional 0.9 billion for buildings and infrastructure (currency word garbled in the transcript) and an incremental $0.6 billion in machinery; '2/3 of the increase of our CapEx is for building and facilities', as a suitable new factory or facility is 'one of the gating factors for us to expand'; this year's machinery capex 'should be sufficient to support another 10% growth' in LEAP services. The two recently acquired buildings will both be for LEAP services, ramping progressively from early 2027; building work starts earlier, equipment from 2027 once the space is vacated. Q1 machinery and equipment capex was USD 1 billion ($636 million packaging, $327 million testing, $40 million EMS, $1 million interconnect materials and others) plus TWD 771 million on facilities. CFO: 'next year is could be another CapEx heavy year for us' (capex growing next year: 'It's more likely, yes'), and 'I wouldn't preclude that there will be further need for us to increase our CapEx for the year' as forecasts are being adjusted rapidly. IR: depreciation is rising faster than revenues in 2026 because LEAP lines must be installed at scale as a full set of machinery and take longer to bring up and tune.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex +0.9B buildings and +$0.6B machinery; Q1 machinery capex USD 1B; Q1 facilities TWD 771M

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY AND DEMAND (IR head Kenneth Hsiang): blended factory utilization was around 80% in Q1, which 'can be slightly misleading' — loading was a little better, but LEAP capacity being installed (revenue weighted towards Q4) and the consolidation of traditional capacity bring the blended rate down. 'Our capacities, along with those of our upstream foundry partners, are finite with limited ability to be pulled forward at this point'; demand is strong not only for LEAP but also for wire bond and traditional advanced packaging, and customers prefer manufacturing certainty on the timing and pricing of wafers, substrates, packaging and testing. ATM revenue grew sequentially despite Q1 seasonality, as AI-related products 'do not appear to follow the same seasonal patterns'. CFO Joseph Tung: Q1 saw stronger than normal seasonal demand, 'maybe coming from pull-in', but 'we don't have the capacity to entertain those pulling demands' and he does not think pull-ins bumped up Q1 revenue; he confirmed no meaningful unit-demand weakness versus three months earlier.

Q1 2026 other results: ATM operating profit TWD 15.9 billion, ATM operating margin 14.1% (+4.5 points YoY); ATM gross margin 26% was down 0.3 points QoQ on Lunar New Year labor costs and higher depreciation from preparing equipment for expansion. EMS revenue TWD 61.9 billion (-10% QoQ, -1% YoY), EMS gross margin 9.5%, operating margin 3.1%; EMS computing revenue rose on a pickup in new AI accelerator products while communications fell on seasonality. Consolidated EBITDA TWD 38.2 billion; cash equivalents and current financial assets TWD 114 billion; net debt to equity 40%. In the ATM 3C mix, computing (where LEAP services are primarily used) keeps growing as a share while communications declines.
quarterly_data.figure: ATM OM 14.1%; EMS revenue TWD 61.9B (-10% QoQ), EMS GM 9.5%, OM 3.1%; EBITDA TWD 38.2B

quarterly_data.signal: FULL-PROCESS LEAP AND 2027 (CFO Joseph Tung): the full process is on track and ASE still believes it can reach the '300 million dollar revenue mark' this year; capacity is expanding with 'quite substantial growth' expected in 2027, ASE is expanding its customer base there ('multiple customers requesting'), and it believes it can take any application moving into CoWoS-like packages; the full process should 'in theory' be accretive to LEAP margins. On 2027 LEAP, this year's incremental revenue (stated as 2 billion or 1.9 billion) 'is really just to serve as a baseline' — 'we can safely expect even stronger momentum than that', without a number. CPO: 'it's a must-have going forward, but at this point, it's still at a very early stage', 'a bit premature' to say when and how much it will contribute. Panel: the CFO says ASE will 'be the first to start the capacity ramp up' (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: full process ~300 million dollar revenue 2026; 2027 LEAP increment above the 2026 baseline
